newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity falls as generation units return.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity falls as generation units return.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading lower Friday as several Western generation units returned to service, industry sources said.
"We've seen quite a drop based on these unit returns," said one Western power trader.

As of 1220 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) was trading down 51 cents at $35.35 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges at $35.15-35.40, while September was down 60 cents at $29.25 after trades at $29.10-29.40 per MWh.
August California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down 56 cents at $22.35 following exchanges at $22.10-22.40, while September was down 48 cents at $22.35 after trades at $22.30-22.50 per MWh.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 254 PV and 270 COB contracts had traded as of 1145 EDT.
Several generation units in the U.S. West returned to service or were ramping up power to full service as of Friday.
The 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear power unit in Avila Beach on the central California coast was running at 100 percent power following a repair outage that began July 2.
Also, the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state is scheduled to reach full power Monday or Tuesday following repairs to its cooling system.
The Washington Public Power Supply System unit was taken off line early Thursday for the repair work, but its reactor continues to run at about 20 percent capacity.
The 1,070 MW unit 2 and 1,080 MW unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in Southern California were scheduled to restart July 15 and 17, respectively.
However, several units remained off line or were expected to be taken off line in the near future.

The 750 MW unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada remained off line with no estimate as to how long it would be shut. The unit, which tripped off Monday due to a boiler tube leak, had been expected to restart late Wednesday night, but the discovery of additional tube leaks led to the delay.
A 750 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico will be shut today for three weeks for repairs.
Also, the 750 MW unit 1 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Ariz., will be shut from Friday night until early Monday morning for repair work.
Forecasters called for hot, dry weather in the Southwest next week, and a warming trend to begin this weekend in the Pacific Northwest.
Temperatures along the West Coast are expected to average in the 70s-80s F, while those in the interior Southwest would run just above 100 degrees F.
